correctness.rationale: The substitution emits 0 at each even position, and a 1 never has an adjacent 1. The length-three patterns at even and odd starts are disjoint, so counting occurrences of longer factors can be done separately by starting parity. The quarter-length suffix D_(j−2) starts with 010 when its size is at least four, hence each occurrence desubstitutes on even block boundaries until 01 in D₃, which occurs exactly at 0,4,6. Lifting gives 0,2q,3q for q=2^(j−2); right-aligning within those copies gives at least three occurrences of every shorter suffix. For length 2k the even encoding uses all k-factors and the odd one omits just the final k-factor occurrence; for length 2k+1 the even encoding omits that occurrence and the odd encoding uses all (k+1)-factors. Each encoding is injective, and deletion of a suffix occurrence cannot yield a singleton at lengths ≤K=2^(j−3), since that suffix occurs at least three times. In particular length 2K has no singleton; all shorter factors are nonunique because any occurrence extends within the finite word to length 2K. At length 2K+1 only the odd class can be unique and is in exact correspondence with the preceding four starts through i↦2i+1. Direct base case D₃ has starts 1,2,3,5 at length 3. This proves the claim for all n≥3. An independent exact suffix-array/LCP calculation and suffix hit-count check passed at orders 3–14 (`python3 /workspace/branches/frozen_review_checks.py`); that check is not an infinite proof or formal certification.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The attractor theorem concerns factor coverage by positions and does not give singleton multiplicities. The fixed-parity lemma is already in the literature. Arbitrary-word SUS algorithms do not provide this closed form. A generic unrestricted occurrence-preservation hypothesis cannot simply be assumed here: φ(11)=0000 contains three occurrences of φ(1)=00 versus two occurrences of 1 in 11. The decisive dominating coverage is instead the complete classification in a64ede970c54.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Every unique substring contains a factor minimal among its unique subfactors, and a globally shortest unique substring is necessarily minimal.
